extracted.intended_audience: researchers reporting in vivo animal experiments; journal editors and peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist-style reporting guidelines (ARRIVE 2.0) specifying items manuscripts should include when describing animal research to allow assessment of reliability and reproducibility. The items are organised into the 'Essential 10' (minimum required) and a 'Recommended set' (additional best-practice context).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 1 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Basic information on the design of the study that must be reported so readers and reviewers can assess reliability of findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the 'Essential 10' — the basic minimum that must be included in any manuscript describing animal research. Examples of good reporting are provided in the Explanation and Elaboration document and in extracted published examples across model organisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 2 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Information about how sample sizes were decided and reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential 10 item. Guidance and examples are provided in the Explanation and Elaboration; proper sample size reporting helps assess power and risk of type I/II errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 3 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Report criteria for including or excluding animals, data points, or experimental units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential 10 item. Must be stated to permit assessment of potential bias from selective inclusion/exclusion; examples in the E&E document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 4 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Describe if and how randomisation was used to allocate animals to experimental groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential 10 item. Report methods used for random allocation and any restriction; lack of randomisation should be disclosed and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding/Masking
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 5 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Report whether blinding/masking was used during allocation, conduct, and outcome assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential 10 item. Describe who was blinded, at what stages, and how blinding was maintained; if blinding was not done, explain why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 6 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Define all pre-specified primary and secondary outcome measures, including how and when they were assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential 10 item. Clear definition of outcome measures is necessary to interpret results; E&E provides example reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 7 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Report the statistical methods used, including assumptions, model details, and how data met method assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential 10 item. Include software, tests, handling of missing data, and how unit of analysis was chosen; examples and explanations available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 8 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Provide details about the animals used (species, strain, sex, age, weight, source, and other relevant characteristics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential 10 item. Full animal descriptors enable reproducibility and interpretation; see E&E for illustrative examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 9 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Describe procedures in sufficient detail to allow replication (what was done, how, when, and by whom).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential 10 item. Provide step-by-step procedural detail, reagents, equipment, timing, and any welfare-related interventions; supporting examples are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 10 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Report findings with appropriate summary statistics, effect sizes, and measures of variability and uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential 10 item. Include all results relevant to pre-specified outcomes, present summary statistics and confidence intervals where appropriate; examples in E&E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 11 of the Recommended set. Report key study information concisely in the abstract to summarise experimental design and main findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended set — complements the Essential 10 and adds context. Reporting the Recommended items represents best practice; examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 12 of the Recommended set. Provide scientific background and rationale for the study, including relevant literature and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Adds important contextual information to help interpret the study's purpose and approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 13 of the Recommended set. State specific objectives, hypotheses, or research questions addressed by the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Clear articulation of objectives helps define primary outcomes and appropriate analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 14 of the Recommended set. Report ethical approvals, welfare considerations, and oversight relevant to the conduct of animal research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Include approval bodies, protocol numbers, and justification for procedures where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing and husbandry
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 15 of the Recommended set. Provide details on the housing, husbandry, and environmental conditions experienced by animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Report cage type, bedding, light/dark cycles, temperature, enrichment, and other husbandry variables affecting outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal care and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 16 of the Recommended set. Describe welfare monitoring, humane endpoints, analgesia, and any interventions for animal care during the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Report how animals were monitored, criteria for intervention or euthanasia, and pain management strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation/ scientific implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 17 of the Recommended set. Interpret results in the context of the hypotheses, limitations, and broader scientific implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Discuss limitations, potential sources of bias, and how findings relate to existing knowledge and future research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability/ translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 18 of the Recommended set. Discuss the generalisability of findings and their potential translational relevance to other species or clinical settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Consider biological differences, model limitations, and implications for translation to humans or other contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 19 of the Recommended set. Report whether study protocols were registered or pre-specified and where they can be accessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Registration or pre-specification increases transparency and reduces selective reporting; provide registry details if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data access
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 20 of the Recommended set. Provide information on availability of study data, code, and materials to enable reuse and verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. State data repositories, accession numbers, or reasons for restricted access; encourage open data where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 21 of the Recommended set. Disclose funding sources and potential conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Transparent disclosure of financial and non-financial interests helps readers assess potential biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: General guidance and supporting materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Contextual guidance appearing on the page: the ARRIVE guidelines 2.0 Explanation and Elaboration (E&E) was published in PLOS Biology and provides detailed explanations, examples of good reporting, and illustrative examples across model organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidelines are organised into two prioritised sets (Essential 10 and Recommended set). The Essential 10 are the minimum items required for manuscripts; the Recommended set complements them and represents best practice. Examples are regularly expanded; consulting the guidelines during planning helps improve experimental design, minimisation of bias, sample size justification, and statistical analyses. DOI for E&E: 10.1371/journal.pbio.3000411.
